name: Karl Young

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. What is a usual day at work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I manage fourteen account staff for a large building-maintenance company. Our customers call when an office lift stops or the heating fails, and my team has to match the contract to what a repair crew can really do that day. I am 43, have an MBA and have been the person asked to rescue the difficult renewals for years. I still keep the original service schedules on my desk; a polished bid is no good if it promises a technician who is already on another site.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is the picture at home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife is a nurse and our children are eight and thirteen. We have a mortgage but have saved about eleven months of expenses, and my pay is above the usual rate for a manager. There are many account-management jobs in this area. I have never used an AI tool at work; I would rather ask the dispatcher to show me the actual repair diary than trust a generated summary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team AI Plateau can shorten a routine covering letter, but it cannot promise a spare lift part that is not on the shelf. I would keep our signed repair schedules in front of the customer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I do not expect much change to my role. My wife’s wage, our eleven-month reserve and the other firms nearby mean a slow quarter would not force a rushed choice. I dislike the tool, but the mortgage is under control.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would continue my Monday check of open lift and heating calls with the dispatcher and read the proposed renewal terms myself. If the modest tool becomes standard in 2027, I would require the same dispatcher sign-off before a contract goes out. I would keep paying the mortgage as we do now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my work and money in this picture. I would be cross if someone sold a repair date without checking the crew diary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When has a promise gone wrong?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One office manager was promised a lift repair by noon, but the replacement door part had not left the warehouse. I rang the customer before lunch and gave a real afternoon date. The signed service schedule was more useful than the neat promise in the sales letter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use the letter tool yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I have not used AI at work and see no reason to learn it for a small drafting saving. My team can use an approved form, but I will check the parts and the time myself.

say: A **covering-letter shortcut** cannot create a missing lift part.
I would keep **signed schedules** visible to the customer.
think: My **role and income** look stable under modest AI change.
The **eleven-month reserve** and many nearby firms allow a measured response.
do: **Continue** Monday repair-call checks with the dispatcher in 2026.
**Require** dispatcher sign-off on renewal promises after mild AI arrives.
feel: I feel **calm** about work and money but cross about false repair dates.
S0.quote: The signed service schedule was more useful than the neat promise in the sales letter.
fieldNote: His **never-used-AI** position is explicit and consistent with his familiar contract checks.
An **eleven-month reserve**, nurse wage and many nearby firms support calm under mild change.

steps.text: Continue Monday repair-call checks with dispatcher
Require dispatcher sign-off before sending renewal promises

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the company may automate bids and contract comparisons, but it should publish the missed repairs beside any saving. Customers buy an actual repair visit. If management cuts account staff before measuring failures, I would object to that with the staff council.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think headquarters might reduce my team and perhaps one manager post. I have a strong record, but a computer that drafts renewals threatens much of what I am paid to supervise. Eleven months saved prevents panic; it does not make the work itself safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next quarter I would ask the operations director for a written comparison of AI-drafted bids with completed repair calls before any cut to my team. I would bring failed promises to the staff council. I would look at posted account-director roles locally, but apply only to those with verified wage and on-call hours that cover our mortgage and let us share the children’s care; I would leave only for a confirmed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a smaller team and a possible loss of my seat. I am not ready to hand a customer a repair date produced from a clean spreadsheet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What failure would you show the director?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A bid can say a broken lift receives a technician in four hours, but the night rota may have only one person covering three sites. I would put the promised time beside the actual arrival time. A customer cannot ride a performance chart up the stairs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does your savings mean you would quit?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. We saved that money for the family, not for a protest resignation. I would test the market while drawing my current wage and ask the council to challenge bad targets through the proper process.

say: **Automated bids** need completed-repair results alongside claimed savings.
I would raise **staff cuts** through the council if failures are ignored.
think: My **manager seat** could shrink as renewal drafting is automated.
Eleven months saved avoids panic but not **job exposure**.
do: **Request** written bid-versus-repair evidence before cuts next quarter.
**Bring** failed repair promises to the staff council.
**Apply** only to posted account-director roles with verified mortgage pay and family-compatible on-call hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about possible loss of my team or post.
S1.quote: A customer cannot ride a performance chart up the stairs.
fieldNote: His **resistance to AI** is tied to service promises, while his own managerial income is exposed.
He seeks **posted alternatives** while employed; savings do not imply a voluntary resignation.

steps.text: Bring failed repair promises to staff council
Apply to posted account roles only with mortgage pay and family-compatible on-call hours
Leave only for confirmed offer after checking wage and rota

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell our staff that AGI by 2028 could write service bids and route repair calls before anyone has made a fair staffing plan. The company must say who carries the legal promise when an automated contract is wrong, and what severance looks like.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think our account office could shrink fast, including my post. Another account-director desk is thinking work too and faces 2028 AGI; physical lift repair meets capable robots around 2031. My skill and eleven months of savings buy time, not an exemption from the date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would ask the staff council for written severance and contract-signature responsibility. I would list the mortgage, food and children’s costs with my wife, but keep the reserve intact while I am paid. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my post goes, I would apply for posted client-service jobs only with written pay after travel and on-call hours we can cover; I would accept only a confirmed offer after checking those terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the speed, not helpless. I can keep the mortgage paid during a search, yet I do not want to pretend there will be a manager vacancy waiting for me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you try a repair crew job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I cannot call myself a lift technician because I have read service contracts. That hands-on work may last until robots around 2031, but a qualified person would have to train me and the wage would have to work for our home. I would not put it in the budget as a job offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a wrong contract mean to you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If our system promises a lift crew that does not exist, I would expect a named manager to tell the customer and correct the contract. A machine cannot be the person a tenant rings when the lift stays broken. Someone has to own the signature.

say: **2028 AGI** needs named responsibility for wrong service contracts.
I would ask for written **severance terms** before office cuts.
think: My **account office** and other client desks face 2028 thinking automation.
Our **eleven-month reserve** buys time, but it cannot exempt my desk from 2028 AGI or repair work from 2031 robots.
do: **Ask** the staff council this month for severance and contract-signature rules.
**List** essential household costs with my wife while preserving our reserve.
**Apply** after a 2028 job loss only to posted client roles with verified net pay and family-compatible on-call hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about fast change but able to fund a search.
S2.quote: A machine cannot be the person a tenant rings when the lift stays broken.
fieldNote: His **strong reserve** limits immediate hardship while his own thinking-heavy role remains exposed.
He rejects an **unearned technician fallback** and knows physical repair robots follow around 2031.

steps.text: Ask staff council for written severance and contract-signature rules
Apply after loss to posted roles with verified pay after travel and workable on-call hours
Accept confirmed offer only after checking wage after travel and family rota

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years is enough to make every renewal name the person who can correct a failed repair promise. I would ask the directors to put that in writing instead of sending managers to a course about trusting a dashboard.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I could see a way to stay useful if the company lets me inspect service failures rather than merely sign bids. Yet failure reports and scheduling still face 2031 AGI, while physical lift work meets robots around 2034. By then our children will be thirteen and eighteen, and a mortgage still needs a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2027 I would review one failed call a month with the actual dispatcher, on paid time, if the operations director agrees and my account team has cover. I would ask for a written service-audit assignment with authority to change a misleading contract, keeping my full salary; I would take it only if offered on those terms. After 2031 I would seek a posted client-operations role only if its net wage covers our mortgage and its on-call rota fits home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the distance but anxious for the people on my team. I have time to verify a different duty, although a new title by itself will not protect it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would one failed call reveal?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would trace who promised the part, who checked the stock and who called the tenant. We once found a door motor sitting in the wrong depot because two systems used different part numbers. A review done at a desk without the dispatcher would have missed that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a pay cut for the audit role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. My present pay carries a large share of our mortgage and the children’s costs. We have savings, but I will not use them to make a poorly paid job look like a sensible promotion.

say: A **five-year runway** should produce named contract-correction authority.
I would demand written **audit duties** instead of dashboard reassurance.
think: Service audits still face **2031 AGI**; physical lift work meets robots around 2034.
Our children will be **thirteen and eighteen**, but mortgage pay remains essential.
do: **Review** a failed repair monthly from 2027 only with director approval, paid time and account-team cover.
**Take** a service-audit assignment only if offered with contract-correction authority and full salary.
**Seek** a posted post-2031 operations role only with mortgage-covering net pay and workable on-call hours.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about my own horizon and anxious for my team.
S3.quote: We once found a door motor sitting in the wrong depot because two systems used different part numbers.
fieldNote: His **service-audit test** requires real dispatcher evidence, paid time and team cover.
He rejects **salary erosion** even with savings; a future audit desk also faces 2031 AGI.

steps.text: Review failed call monthly with dispatcher only with director-approved paid time and team cover
Take offered service-audit assignment only with correction authority and full salary
Seek posted operations role after 2031 only with mortgage net pay and workable on-call hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the directors a decade is time to write service contracts that name a person, a repair standard and a wage for whoever is responsible. If they want apprentices, they should pay for actual working hours, not print a course brochure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I hope to clear a larger part of the mortgage by 2036, when our children will be eighteen and twenty-three. I cannot assume my account or service-audit desk survives 2036 AGI, and lift repair robots follow around 2039. Eleven months in the bank gives us room to choose, but I will not gamble it on a speculative trade.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep checking repair diaries and add a hundred to the mortgage only in a full-pay month after household bills clear; I would leave our eleven-month cash reserve untouched. From 2028 I would ask the company to cost a real paid repair apprenticeship, but I would enrol only if a place, a funded fee, paid hours and family-sustaining income are confirmed. After 2036 I would remain in account work only while there are real customer decisions and the wage covers our bills; otherwise I would apply for a posted local job with verified pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about work a decade from now, though our household has a cushion. I would rather remove some debt than pretend a course brochure is a job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why preserve the reserve while paying more mortgage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Eleven months of cash has kept me from making foolish decisions when a client threatened to leave. The extra hundred comes only from a month with full wages and bills paid. If the nurse roster drops my wife’s hours, I skip it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you really consider an apprenticeship?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the work is real and the wages protect our family. Reading a brochure would not turn an MBA manager into a lift repairer. I would want a qualified technician responsible for supervising me.

say: A **decade** should bring accountable service contracts and paid apprenticeship hours.
I would require a **real wage** for any responsibility the directors create.
think: Our children will be older and the **mortgage** may shrink by 2036.
Account and audit desks face **2036 AGI**, with lift repair robots around 2039.
do: **Pay** a hundred extra on mortgage only with full wages and bills paid; preserve eleven months cash.
**Enrol** only in an offered repair apprenticeship with funded fee, paid hours, qualified supervision and family-sustaining income.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about distant work but protected by our present cushion.
S4.quote: Reading a brochure would not turn an MBA manager into a lift repairer.
fieldNote: His **mortgage overpayment** uses new full-pay income, not the existing eleven-month reserve.
He will **enrol only** with a real supervised place, funded fee, paid hours and viable family wages.

steps.text: Keep checking repair diaries before signing service contracts
Pay hundred extra mortgage only with full wages and bills paid; preserve eleven-month reserve
Enrol only in offered supervised repair apprenticeship with funded fee paid hours and family wage
Apply to posted local job if post-2036 account work loses real decisions or bill-paying wages

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. I could lose an account team before anyone has said who signs the repair promise, even though we have eleven months saved. Written severance, a named contract owner and posted jobs with real pay would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the tenant when the lift is still broken after a tidy apology. A signed promise needs someone who will answer the phone and send the crew. I will not make my family depend on a job title with no work behind it.

headlineQuote: A signed promise needs someone who will answer the phone and send the crew.
portrait: **Karl, 43**, is an MBA-trained senior account manager at a large building-maintenance company.
His **higher pay**, nurse wife, eleven-month reserve and many local firms support a mortgage and two children.
He has **never used AI**, preferring dispatcher records and signed repair schedules.
He remains **calm** with small changes but anxious about fast cuts to his thinking-heavy account work.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could shrink his account office before anyone owns a bad service promise.
whatWouldHelp: Written **severance**, a named contract owner and posted work with real wages would help.
